key_insight: Penalizing order-k derivatives of the velocity makes empirical flow matching uniformly well posed in time when 2k > D and training points are in general position.
engineering_relevance: Explicit derivative regularization offers a principled way to stabilize flow matching against memorization and sensitivity to discretization.
method: Regularize velocity derivatives rather than velocity magnitude alone.
Discretize velocity fields with splines in one and two dimensions.
Use direct solvers for regularized least squares to exclude optimization error.
evidence_signal: In 1D and 2D experiments, Hessian-regularized flows showed only marginal error changes under space-time refinement and achieved errors comparable to or lower than well-tuned kernel density estimates.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to low-dimensional spline models; the condition 2k > D requires higher-order derivative penalties as dimension increases.
